s1.syndrome_frame: Severe systemic toxicity with hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Severe hyperthermia with temperature of 107°F
Rhabdomyolysis with severe kidney injury
Agitation, confusion, and altered mental status
History of ingestion and insufflation of 'bath salts'
Severe cardiovascular instability with hypotension and tachycardia
key_facts: 29-year-old Caucasian man
History of hepatitis C, posttraumatic stress disorder, polysubstance abuse, and tobacco use
Found agitated and erratically wandering the streets
Reported ingestion and insufflation of 'bath salts'
Denied other medications or supplements
No known drug allergies
Temperature of 107°F on examination
Blood pressure 91/52 mm Hg and pulse 93/min
Confused and intermittently agitated with pupils 3 mm and equal
Weak peripheral pulses without jugular venous distention or murmurs
Laboratory studies showed features of severe rhabdomyolysis
Serologic testing confirmed chronic hepatitis C
Serum toxicology tests were negative for ethanol, acetaminophen, and salicylates
Urine toxicology detected lorazepam and cotinine
Received aggressive IV fluids, norepinephrine infusion, and other treatments

shortlist.label: Sympathomimetic toxicity
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of agitation, hyperthermia, and rhabdomyolysis are consistent with sympathomimetic toxicity, and the patient reported ingestion of 'bath salts' which can cause this condition

shortlist.label: Serotonin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of confusion, agitation, and hyperthermia are also consistent with serotonin syndrome, and some 'bath salts' can cause serotonin release

shortlist.label: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of hyperthermia, confusion, and muscle rigidity (rhabdomyolysis) are similar to those of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, although the patient did not report taking neuroleptics

shortlist.label: Malignant hyperthermia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's severe hyperthermia and rhabdomyolysis could be consistent with malignant hyperthermia, although this condition is typically associated with anesthesia or succinylcholine use

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis due to drug-induced immobilization
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's rhabdomyolysis could be due to immobilization caused by the effects of 'bath salts', and this diagnosis is consistent with the patient's symptoms and lab results
